prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1108; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Received first notice of loss from the insured driver by phone. Insured reports a sideswipe while changing lanes on a multi-lane roadway. Other vehicle reportedly drifted into the insured's lane and made contact with the rear quarter panel. Insured states the other driver left the scene before exchanging information. Photos of insured vehicle requested. Police report number not yet obtained.

Entry 2: Spoke with insured's passenger, who reports neck and back pain following the impact. Passenger has been advised to seek medical evaluation and keep all treatment records. Claim file updated to reflect a bodily injury component. Counsel for the claimant has since contacted the desk and requested that all communications go through their office.

Entry 3: Reviewed photos and repair estimate from the body shop. Damage is consistent with the reported sideswipe, with scrape marks and a cracked taillight lens on the rear quarter. Estimate is under review. Liability remains disputed because the other driver has not been identified and the witness statement is still pending.

Entry 4: Received a letter from the claimant's attorney asserting neck and back strain and requesting medical authorization forms. Forms sent to counsel with a note that the carrier will evaluate medical bills once received. Requested the claimant's prior claims history and medical records for the affected areas. Reserve adjusted to reflect the injury exposure.

Entry 5: Follow-up call with claimant's counsel regarding treatment status. Counsel confirms the claimant is attending physical therapy for the neck and back strain and expects to provide itemized bills. Diary set for review in thirty days. Liability investigation continues, including canvass for the unidentified vehicle and any dashcam footage from nearby traffic.
